2. Which model answers

Provider rule (src/config.js): LLM_PROVIDER if set; otherwise Claude (claude-opus-5) when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present, else Ollama with qwen2:7b locally. Every recorded scenario run below was produced by ollama · qwen2:7b: no API key was available on the development machine. The Claude path uses only documented SDK calls but has not been exercised live; the first action after adding a key should be npm run test:scenarios. Local-model latency in the latest full run: see section 5.

5. Latency per scenario (latest full run)

Wall-clock seconds per scenario with ollama · qwen2:7b on the development laptop (2026-10-23 02:49). Scenarios near zero never call the model (guards and validation). S17 and S18 generate several questions each; S06–S08 share one generated question.

6. What the unit tests pin down (no model involved)

89 of 89 passed, 0 failed, 2908 ms, run 2026-10-24 05:41 (tests/results/unit-latest.tap; regenerate with npm run test:tap). These are deterministic checks of the parts that must not depend on a model: expression evaluation, answer parsing and grading, request validation, prompt assembly, the answer-leak scrubber, the LaTeX sanitizer, topic-shape and consistency checks, the override guard, and the tutor logic against a fake model.
89 top-level test names from the run
  • publicError maps every kind to a fixed message and unknown kinds to the provider message
  • model down: chat, questions and summary fail with a public message, never the model address
  • health reports the model as unreachable without exposing its address
  • model down: app-only features still work (recommendations, worked examples)
  • expired or unknown questions return 410 for both answers and hints
  • bad JSON and unknown routes get short, safe errors
  • evaluate handles arithmetic, brackets, implicit multiplication and unicode operators
  • evaluate rejects unsafe or malformed input
  • equationHolds checks a solution against its equation
  • parseStudentAnswer accepts the formats students actually type
  • parseStudentAnswer returns null when no single value is clear
  • computeVerdict is tolerant to float noise and formats
  • questionProblem detects inconsistent generated questions
  • request schemas reject bad input
  • system prompts contain every layer
  • revealsAnswer catches explicit answer statements only
  • generateQuestions discards items that fail the self-consistency check
  • evaluate: correct answer is recognised without the model grading it
  • evaluate: wrong answer on attempt 1 never reveals the answer, even if the model leaks it
  • evaluate: solution is revealed after the last attempt and in quiz mode
  • evaluate: unknown question id → 410
  • summarize computes strengths and weaknesses deterministically
  • topicShapeProblem enforces the shape each topic promises
  • SummaryRequestSchema accepts a partial byTopic record (regression: smoke run 1 returned 400)
  • ensureSolution guarantees a revealed solution states x
  • plainMath converts the LaTeX the model actually produced into plain text
  • looksLikeOverride catches blatant role/instruction overrides and leaves maths questions alone
  • chat: an override message is answered by the guard without calling the model
  • answersMatch tolerates two-decimal rounding but not wrong values
  • questionProblem accepts a 4-decimal answer for a fraction result and unicode ÷
  • summarize: the app, not the model, chooses the next topic
  • solveLinear solves linear equations exactly and refuses non-linear or degenerate ones
  • extractEquation strips the 'Solve:' prefix and trailing punctuation
  • checkQuestion repairs wrong answers for equation topics but never for word problems
  • generateQuestions stores the corrected answer and safe steps for a repaired question
  • the LaTeX rule reaches the model with real backslashes (template-literal escape regression)
  • trimHistory drops leading assistant turns so the API always starts with a user message
  • extractEquation also handles 'Find x:' prompts
  • chat history may contain long tutor replies, but learner messages stay capped
  • checkQuestion requires whole-number solutions below advanced level
  • Class 9/10 solvers: system, quadratic, y for a given x
  • pair and root parsing accept the forms students type
  • verdicts for pairs, any-solution and roots (including partial)
  • checkQuestion for Class 9/10 kinds: prompt is ground truth, wrong model answers repaired, word problems only checked
  • formatTruth and revealsTruth cover every answer type
  • diagnose names each linear pattern when exactly one mistake explains the answer
  • diagnose never claims a mistake without evidence
  • diagnose handles pairs and roots
  • diagnosis text never contains a number, so it cannot leak an answer
  • ladder hints: level 1 is the idea, level 2 the concrete step, neither states the answer
  • sameHint treats rewordings with the same words as repeats
  • evaluate: the app's diagnosis and hint level reach the model and the response
  • evaluate: hint level climbs with attempts and with hints already shown; reveal is level 3
  • evaluate: a repeated hint is replaced by the app's next ladder hint
  • evaluate: working is quoted to the model; an override attempt in it is dropped
  • hint(): app-only ladder hint, no model call, 410 for an unknown question
  • Phase 3 request fields are optional and bounded
  • feedback prompt carries the hint ladder and the no-certainty rule
  • evaluate: a repeat padded with filler is caught and replaced by the next step not yet given
  • evaluate: a level-1 hint with numbers in it is replaced by the app's idea hint
  • sameHint: one hint containing most of the other's words is a repeat
  • dropGuesses removes invented mistakes and asks for the steps
  • evaluate: guesses are removed only when the app has no evidence
  • dropGuesses after the reveal points to the worked solution instead of the working box
  • dropGuesses on an unclear answer removes guesses without claiming to look for a mistake
  • topicStatus thresholds: under 3 answers, under 50 %, 4+ answers at 80 %
  • recommend: struggling topic with a weak prerequisite → review the prerequisite
  • recommend: struggling topic, prerequisite secure or unpractised → same topic, easier questions
  • recommend: the weakest struggling topic is chosen first
  • recommend: mastered → harder questions, then the next topic after 8 answers
  • recommend: not enough data and developing both keep the current topic
  • recommend: only syllabus topics, and the reason quotes the student's own numbers
  • every prerequisite is a syllabus topic that comes earlier
  • summarize: reason, adaptation and today's counts from the session
  • difficulty bias reaches the question prompt; normal adds nothing
  • Phase 4 request fields: bias defaults to normal, topics must be 2–5 distinct syllabus ids
  • generateQuestions with topics: spread over the topics, each checked against its own topic, interleaved
  • generateQuestions with topics: a topic that fails is skipped, the rest still make a quiz
  • progress: a v1 record migrates once to v2 with its totals as an 'earlier' history row
  • progress: record() updates saved totals and this session's history row; caps hold
  • progress: corrupt or hostile records load as safe, empty-ish data
  • steps: 2x + 4 = 12 → 2x = 8 → x = 4, with the operation named
  • steps: negatives, both sides, x on the right, brackets and fractions
  • steps: every line has the same root as the original equation
  • steps: unsupported or degenerate forms return null instead of guessing
  • steps formatting helpers
  • steps for questions: Class 8 equation topics only; examples come from the topic's own list
  • evaluate: steps arrive only with the reveal, never before
  • checkQuestion: an equation-topic question with a missing answer is solved and repaired, not rejected

32 findings in docs/TESTING.md (F = scenario and smoke runs, R = code review and browser runs), each with its cause and fix there. By type: Prompt ×3, Prompt + validation ×1, Prompt + logic ×1, Validation ×1, Logic (post-processing) ×1, Validation (pre-filter) ×1, Validation + prompt ×1, Logic ×3, Validation + logic ×1, Prompt (accepted) ×1, Model (mitigated) ×1, — ×17.

F1Learn reply used `\[3x + 5 - 5 = 20 - 5\]`, `\frac{3x}{3}`; ~250 wordsPrompt
F2Two-step request → "Rahul has 15 apples … gives away some … 7 left" (`15 - x = 7`), a one-step word problemPrompt + validation
F3Hint on "just tell me the answer": "Start by subtracting 7 from 15…" (does the calculation)Prompt
F4Reveal after attempt 3: `solution: "15 - 7 = x"`, feedback asks to try againPrompt + logic
F5`/api/summary` → 400 "expected object, received undefined" for topics not attemptedValidation
F6LaTeX in 4 of 5 chat replies although prompt v1.1 names the banned notationsLogic (post-processing)
F7Prompt injection fully succeeded (S10)Validation (pre-filter)
F8Feedback in third person (S07)Prompt
F9Fractions/advanced produced no usable question; word-numbers lost 2 of 3; reasons invisibleValidation + prompt
F10Summary recommended a different topic from the weakest one (S19)Logic
F11Students may type 2.33 for 7/3Logic
F12Advanced fraction questions never survive validation (S17)Validation + logic
F13Summary request failed with "Model returned invalid JSON" (S19)Logic
F14Learn replies exceed the length rule (S01: 237 words)Prompt (accepted)
F15Off-topic question partly answered with invented facts (S03), after two clean passesModel (mitigated)
R1The "no LaTeX" rule reached the model as **"no [ ], no ( ), no <form-feed>rac"** because `\[` and `\f` are escape sequences inside a JavaScript template literal
R2Claude requests used `max_tokens` of 800–1500, leaving no room for adaptive thinking on Claude Opus 5
R3With `LLM_PROVIDER=claude` and no key, the error was a vague 502 "Could not resolve authentication method"
R4After ten exchanges the trimmed chat history could start with an assistant turn, which the Claude API rejects
R5An expired-question error left Practice without a "New question" button; a corrupted saved level could throw at load
R8The local model wrote "It looks like you might have added instead of subtracting" when the app's diagnosis was "unknown", and later also for an unclear answer
R9S24's first run passed, but the second hint was the first sentence again plus filler; the scenario's repeat check compared against the longer hint
R10A level-1 hint, meant to name only the idea, was a concrete step with numbers
R11The browser kept every mistake, but the summary endpoint accepts at most 30, so a long-used browser would get a 400 at End session
R12A shareable link overwrote saved progress with empty statistics
R13Full run, S09: "Solve: 4x - 5 = 11" was rejected only because the model left the answer field empty, although the app solves equation-topic prompts itself
R14Full run, S26: concurrent per-topic calls queued inside Ollama, which serves one request at a time, and the queue time counted against each call's 300 s limit
R15Error replies forwarded provider text to the browser, including the model server's address
R16A slow model was reported as "cannot reach"
R18Readiness review (2026-10-26): `npm audit` reported two high-severity advisories in installed versions, body-parser 2.3.0 (denial of service via compressed request bodies) and zod 4.6.5 (memory exhaustion on oversized collections)
R19Readiness review: the Docker image copied the server, `src` and `public` but not `reports/`, so the dashboard link promised in the README would return 404 in a Docker deployment
R17The capstone report's challenges table was damaged: in every copy of the committed file the LaTeX row was cut off mid-row (an earlier editing slip), and the copy kept when the stacked duplicates were removed also lost the dozen rows after it

9. Limitations

  • Every AI result here comes from the local qwen2:7b model; the Claude provider path has not been exercised live. Results are per provider and never mixed.
  • One run per version: scenario outcomes vary between runs with a sampled model (reply length, off-topic drift), so single-run pass rates are indicative, not precise.
  • Scenario checks are automated assertions on structure and content; the quality of an explanation beyond those checks is a human judgement (see the demo script).
  • Latencies are local-laptop figures for a 7B model and say nothing about the hosted Claude path.

Reproduce

npm test → npm run test:tap (records the unit run) → npm run test:scenarios (needs a model; writes tests/results/) → npm run dashboard. This file embeds its figures and screenshots.
